verdict: Tesla's revenue rose 8% to $25.2B and operating income jumped 54% to $2.7B, as cost cuts and a booming energy business outweighed lower car prices — net income rose 17% to $2.2B.

segments.name: Automotive
segments.note: Selling and leasing cars, plus $739M of regulatory credits — deliveries rose 6% to 462,890, but lower average prices held revenue growth to 2%.

segments.name: Energy generation and storage
segments.note: Megapack batteries and solar — deployments hit 6.9 GWh, up 75% YoY, and the energy business earned a record 30.5% gross margin.

segments.name: Services and other
segments.note: Supercharging, repairs, insurance and used-car sales — gross profit grew over 90% YoY to a record.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: AI, the Optimus robot, Cybercab and new vehicles.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Selling cars and running the company day to day.

opex.name: Restructuring & other
opex.note: One-off costs of reshaping the business — much smaller than the charges taken earlier in 2024.

otherDetail: Interest income of $429M, less $92M of interest expense and $270M of other expense — mostly currency losses — a net +$67M below operating profit.
footerNote: Net income here is Tesla's total net income of $2,183M; $2,167M of it is attributable to common stockholders (the rest belongs to minority partners in subsidiaries). Financial statements are from Tesla's Q3 2024 Form 10-Q; deliveries and deployments are from its October 2, 2024 release.

takeaways.title: Deliveries bounced back
takeaways.text: Tesla delivered 462,890 vehicles, up 6% YoY, and produced 469,796 — but it had cut prices to get there, so automotive revenue rose only 2% to $20.0B.

takeaways.title: Energy is quietly surging
takeaways.text: Energy storage deployments jumped 75% YoY to 6.9 GWh, energy revenue rose 52% to $2.4B, and the energy business earned a record 30.5% gross margin.

takeaways.title: Cost cuts widened margins
takeaways.text: Operating income rose 54% YoY to $2.7B as the gross margin widened to 19.8% from 17.9% a year ago — cost reductions per car more than offset the price cuts.

oneTimers: Self-driving revenue recognised early: Tesla recognised $326M of Full Self-Driving revenue in the quarter for Cybertruck and features such as Actually Smart Summon — money customers had paid earlier, booked as revenue when the features shipped.
